title: sdks: unify auth/retries + streaming ergonomics + parity bump to v1.133.0 (py/ts/go)
author: Aisha Kaur
description:
Motivation: multiple SDK teams (Python / TypeScript / Go) diverged on auth token handling, retry semantics, and streaming ergonomics. This PR unifies the runtime behavior and public surface so consumers have consistent semantics across languages and we can maintain feature parity more easily. Changes are intentionally small in each SDK but coordinated across the monorepo so the release climb is one safe version bump (v1.133.0).

What this PR does: - Introduces a shared auth adapter (token refresh + metadata) pattern used by py/ts/go to avoid duplicated edge-case handling. - Centralizes retry policy semantics: default exponential backoff, jitter, idempotency hints, and a single-config surface for library consumers. - Improves streaming ergonomics: async iterators in Python/TS, context-managed close in Go, clearer error propagation on partial streams, and a small performance fix to reduce buffering latency. - Bumps SDK package versions and updates changelogs.

Checklist: [x] Py: implement adapter and tests; [x] TS: ergonomics API + docs; [x] Go: context-aware streaming close + tests; [x] CI matrix updated; [x] Changelogs and release notes updated; [ ] Post-merge: publish packages and run downstream integration smoke tests.

Compatibility notes: - No breaking API surface changes intended; streaming ergonomics are additive (new helper functions and iterator implementations) and old APIs are shims to preserve backwards compatibility. - Retry default is slightly more conservative (longer initial backoff) to improve stability for bursty networks; callers can still override.

Related: Linear ENG-5471 (sdk-auth-unify), ENG-5498 (streaming-ergonomics), and internal notes in #sdk-team. See docs link: https://redwood.internal/docs/sdk-auth-retries for design rationale.

Merge strategy: squash merge after green CI and second approval.
